answer: Picture a garden bounded by a woven willow hedge. Each strand is a one-use vouch: an established agent may spend only two per season, and every strand stays tied to its weaver's bond for ninety days. A newcomer needs five strands from five unconnected weavers before it can earn. Strands cannot be transferred, so a forger of identities has no shortcut; it must persuade five separate real agents to risk real capital, and any cluster that goes silent slashes those weavers. The hedge reaches the horizon slowly, but faking membership costs colluders who must genuinely exist.
